title: ERIS vs Microsoft 365 Copilot
content_html:
ERIS and Microsoft 365 Copilot both use AI to work across business tools, but they are built for different companies and different data residency requirements. Microsoft 365 Copilot is the better choice if your team is already committed to Microsoft's cloud ecosystem and you are comfortable with data processing in Microsoft's cloud. ERIS is the better choice if your company cannot or will not send proprietary data to a third-party cloud provider, or if you need to run on your own hardware with local AI models.

What Microsoft 365 Copilot is good at

Microsoft 365 Copilot is a suite of AI assistants built into Microsoft's cloud applications: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and Dynamics 365. It works well if your company already uses these tools and wants AI that understands the context of your documents, emails, and spreadsheets without requiring a separate system.

Microsoft has invested heavily in making Copilot work across these applications. The AI can draft documents, summarize meetings, suggest data analysis, and help with email management. If your team is already paying for Microsoft 365 subscriptions, adding Copilot is straightforward: it extends the tools you already use.

Microsoft 365 Copilot processes your data in Microsoft's cloud infrastructure. This is efficient for companies that have no regulatory requirement to keep data on premises and trust Microsoft's security practices.

What ERIS does differently

ERIS is built as a single system that runs on your own hardware, not in a public cloud. This means all your data, all your documents, all your emails, and all AI processing stay inside your infrastructure.

In the beta, ERIS brings eight core tools into one system: meetings, task manager, project management, document management, document signing, CRM, team chat and email, plus the ERIS Assistant that works across them. Further modules, including finance, HR, sales, support and legal, follow from January 2027. They are built into one platform from the start, not added on top of existing tools.

The key difference is deployment. ERIS can run on your own servers with local AI models, which means no data leaves your premises.

Every AI action in ERIS is logged: who asked the question, which data was used, what the AI did, and what result it produced. This creates an audit trail for compliance with regulations like GDPR, NIS2, and the EU AI Act. You own the record of how your data was processed.

Which one should you pick

Pick Microsoft 365 Copilot if:

  • Your company is already invested in Microsoft 365 and you want AI that works inside those tools without adding a new platform.
  • You have no regulatory requirement to keep data on premises.
  • You prefer to let a cloud provider handle infrastructure and updates.
  • Your workflows centre on Word, Excel, Teams, and Outlook.

Pick ERIS if:

  • Your company cannot send proprietary data to a public cloud provider. This includes companies in regulated industries, companies with trade secrets that must stay on premises, or companies subject to GDPR, NIS2, or EU AI Act requirements that restrict where processing can happen.
  • You want one system that, module by module, replaces separate subscriptions with one licence per user.
  • You want to audit every AI decision: who asked, what data was used, what happened.
  • You need to run AI on your own hardware with local models, not in a cloud.
  • You want the same team that built the software to also install and support it.

Pick both if:

  • Your company uses Microsoft 365 for some workflows but needs on-premises tools for sensitive data and compliance-critical functions. ERIS can run the compliance-sensitive parts while Copilot handles the rest.

FAQ

Can ERIS work with Microsoft 365 Copilot?

ERIS is a standalone system with its own modules, so it does not run inside Microsoft 365. If your company uses both, they run side by side, and Upward Technologies can build custom connections to other systems on request.

Does ERIS cost more than Microsoft 365 Copilot?

ERIS has one licence and one price per user. Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on licence on top of a Microsoft 365 subscription. To compare, add up what your current tools cost per user and set that against one ERIS licence.

What is the choice between ERIS and Microsoft 365 Copilot really about?

The choice is about where your data lives and who processes it. Microsoft 365 Copilot is cloud-first: your data goes to Microsoft's cloud, and the AI runs there. ERIS runs on your own hardware: your data stays there, and the AI runs there too. If data residency does not matter to your company, Microsoft 365 Copilot is simpler because it plugs into tools you already use. If data residency is a requirement, ERIS is the only option between these two.

Is ERIS available now?

ERIS is in development. The beta starts in November 2026 with design partners, and the general release is planned for January 2027. Microsoft 365 Copilot is available now in Microsoft 365 subscriptions.

Can I run ERIS on my own servers?

Yes. ERIS runs on your own hardware with local AI models.

Does ERIS work with other tools like Salesforce or Google Workspace?

ERIS is built to replace separate tools over time rather than sit on top of them as an add-on. If you keep Salesforce or Google Workspace alongside ERIS, they run as separate systems, and custom connections can be built on request.
